coding_rule: Awarded if: Cases were diagnosed with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) based on validated clinical guidelines (e.g., AASLD/EASL) or confirmed by liver biopsy.
Not awarded if: Diagnosis was based solely on self-report or was not clearly defined.
Awarded if: Cases were consecutively enrolled or were a representative sample (e.g., multicentre study).
Not awarded if: There was potential selection bias or the sampling strategy was not described.
Awarded if: Controls were selected from the same community or hospital population as the cases and clearly excluded other liver diseases.
Not awarded if: Source of controls was not described or derived from a different population.
Awarded if: Absence of liver disease was confirmed by medical history and biochemical analysis (e.g., normal ALT/AST levels).
Not awarded if: Based on self-report of "no disease" only.

item: ①Comparability of cohorts on the basis of the design or analysis (Basic)
coding_rule: Awarded if: The study controlled for age and sex (either by matching or statistical adjustment).

item: ②Comparability of cohorts on the basis of the design or analysis (Additional)
coding_rule:
Awarded if: The study controlled for recent antibiotic use (critical), BMI, or dietary habits.
Note: No star is awarded if the study failed to report exclusion or adjustment for antibiotic use (typically within 1–3 months).
Awarded if: Sample collection, DNA extraction, and sequencing platforms (e.g., 16S rRNA sequencing or metagenomic sequencing) were clearly described and are standard methods.

item: ②Same method of ascertainment for cases and controls
coding_rule: Awarded if: Both cases and controls used the identical DNA extraction kits, sequencing regions (e.g., V3-V4), and platforms to avoid batch effects.

item: ②Same method of ascertainment for cases and controls
coding_rule: Not awarded if: Methods differed between groups or were not described.
Awarded if: Non-response rates were similar between groups, or exclusion rates and reasons were comparable.
Not awarded if: Non-response rates differed between groups or were not reported.

High quality ≥ 7 stars
Moderate quality 4–6 stars
Low quality < 4 stars
